Chief_Complaint.content: Dry, itchy skin on arms and hands

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Rash started a few days ago
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Onset: started a few days ago

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Rash located on arms and mainly hands
Skin on affected areas is quite red
Patient denies spread of rash to chest
Patient denies spread of rash to legs
Patient denies spread of rash to face
Patient used coconut butter for a few days without improvement
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Tx tried: coconut butter x few days → not helped

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient denies spots associated with the rash
Patient reports feeling quite tired and run-down
Patient is eating and drinking as normal with fine appetite
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: PO: eating/drinking as normal; appetite fine

Past_Medical_History.content: No prior skin problems including eczema or dermatitis

Medications.content: Patient is taking Microgynon oral contraceptive pill

Family_History.content: Patient denies family history of skin problems

Social_and_Family_History.content: Patient works as a primary school teacher
Patient reports recent work stress due to long hours and children being annoying
Patient does not use recreational drugs

Assessment.content: Dry pruritic erythematous rash on hands and arms for a few days with onset after swimming and no systemic symptoms, query dermatitis
Assessment.source_text: Dry pruritic erythematous rash on hands/arms x few days, onset after swimming; no systemic sx → ?dermatitis

Plan_of_Care.content: Provide patient information leaflet regarding dermatitis
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Provide pt info leaflet re: dermatitis

Plan_of_Care.content: Prescribe or recommend topical steroid cream for inflammation
Use emollients liberally throughout the day for the next few days
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Emollients liberally throughout day x next few days

Plan_of_Care.content: Consider over-the-counter antihistamines such as Piriton or loratadine for itch
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Consider OTC antihistamines for itch (Piriton or loratadine)

Plan_of_Care.content: Analgesics such as paracetamol are not recommended and would not be helpful
